title: Token variance rollups and anomaly-score indexing for cost+latency
author: Ava Martinez
description:
Motivation: long-tail token cost and latency variance across customers and prompt shapes are causing noisy alerts and slow triage. This PR introduces a compact rollup layer and a lightweight anomaly-score index so on-call can quickly find high-variance cohorts without scanning raw traces.

Summary of changes: adds a token-variance aggregator (per-model, per-route, per-tenant and per-prompt-shape buckets), a daily delta-index for anomaly scoring, an API surface to query cohort scores, dashboard panels, and updated alert rules that use anomaly scores to suppress noisy pages.

What this enables:
- fast queries for top-k variance cohorts (model X route Y tenant Z) without scanning the full span store
- per-tenant anomaly scores that combine token-cost variance and tail-latency percentiles
- alert routing: only escalate if anomaly_score >= threshold AND error-rate or latency-p99 breach
- a new dashboard page: "Token Variance Explorer" that surfaces prompt-shape heatmaps and delta histograms

Checklist: [x] rollup job implementation and scheduler [x] API and index writer [x] dashboard panels + saved queries [x] updated alert rules + unit tests [x] e2e smoke test of query latency

Related work: ties into ENG-1982 (prompt-shape bucketing) and ENG-2041 (alert-noise reduction). Addresses incident SUP-782 where a tenant spike generated 40 redundant pages.

Notes on approach: we chose a lightweight fixed-bucket sketch per key (model+route+tenant+shape) to bound cardinality. The daily delta-index stores the relative change in variance and a normalized anomaly_score computed by an exponential weighting of recent deltas. The API exposes top-k by absolute variance or anomaly_score for quick TTR.

Operational considerations: rollups run in the observability service on a dedicated autoscaled pod pool. Rollup writes go to a compact time-series table sharded by model-region; the anomaly index is stored in a read-optimized column with TTL of 90 days. On deployment, we will backfill 14 days of historical variance from existing token-cost buckets to seed the index.

Performance: rollup job is limited to 300ms per key processing window; initial load uses batching and backpressure to avoid pushing to primary tracing cluster. Query latency for top-k < 250ms in staging under 95th percentile traffic.

Security/Privacy: no raw prompt text is stored; prompt-shape is a hashed shape signature. Tenant IDs are stored as opaque billing IDs to preserve PII boundaries.

Merge decisions: squash-merge after approvals, feature gated behind runtime flag "token_variance_rollup".

review_comments: Ravi Patel: Overall looks good. Can we make the anomaly_score computation deterministic (seeded) so staging reproduces prod behavior?
Author (Ava Martinez): We seed the EWMA with the 14-day backfill median; added note in docs and a test that reproduces score seeding.
Sofia Gomez: The rollup pod may create bursts against the tracing DB during backfill. Suggest rate limiting and a retry budget.
Author: Added backpressure + token bucket limiter in aggregator and a configurable backfill_parallelism knob.
Noah Kim: Alert suppression criteria are safer, but add a TTL for suppressed alerts so we don't permanently mute flapping cohorts.
Author: Added suppression window default = 2h and operator-configurable max_suppressions per day.

release_notes: Add token-variance rollups and anomaly-score index for cost and latency
New Grafana dashboard: Token Variance Explorer
Alert rules updated to use anomaly_score for noise reduction
Backfill script to seed 14 days of history (run by SRE)
notes: This PR prioritized a bounded-cardinality approach (fixed bucket sketch) instead of high-cardinality label explosion. The feature is behind a flag and will be rolled out to 10% of tenants initially. Operator runbook includes steps to disable the flag and to run a quick consistency check between backfill and live rollup outputs.
